blocks.content: An audit is a systematic and independent examination of data, statements, records, operations, and performance of an enterprise for a specified purpose.

rows: Mandatory by law for all companies
Mandatory only for specified classes of companies
Appointed by the Board of Directors
Truth and fairness of financial statements

items: CAG audit provisions are governed by Articles 148 to 151 of the Indian Constitution.
Section 204 mandates Secretarial Audit for all listed companies and specified public companies.
Statutory Auditors are appointed by shareholders under Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Statutory Audit is mandatory for companies under the Companies Act, 2013 to ensure true and fair financial reporting.
Internal Audit focuses on evaluating internal control systems, risk management, and operational efficiency.
Tax Audit under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act is required when business turnover crosses prescribed statutory limits.
Cost Audit under Section 148 is applicable to specified manufacturing and production entities.
CAG conducts government audits under Article 148 of the Constitution of India.
